_meta.purpose: Per-(micro, LC-id) application notes — explain HOW the micro's strategy applies to that specific problem. Surfaced in the UI as the anchor chip's tooltip. Audit batch grows over time; see git log.
_meta.status: Audit pass 6 (mega-pass) — 100% coverage of all 143 micros. Per-problem application notes for every anchored LC problem. Notes are intentionally terse (1 sentence each) to fit the scale; the OPTIMAL approach is called out where the tagged pattern works but isn't the best fit.

complement-lookup.1: Two-Sum unsorted. One pass, deferred insert: check map for (target-x) FIRST, then store x→i. Guarantees we don't pair x with itself.
complement-lookup.167: Two-Sum on SORTED array. Hash works but is suboptimal — converging two-pointer (tp-k-sum) is O(1) space. Listed here for the universal pattern.
complement-lookup.653: Two-Sum in a BST. Two clean approaches: (a) collect inorder→array then complement-lookup; (b) two iterators (inorder + reverse-inorder) converging — O(h) space.
complement-lookup.560: Subarray sum = K with negatives. Prefix-sum + complement: map[prefix] = count; for each prefix, answer += map[prefix-K]; then ++map[prefix]. Same complement-lookup engine over prefix space.
complement-lookup.974: Subarray sum divisible by K. Same prefix+complement, but key on (prefix mod K) (normalise negative mods). The complement is just the SAME residue (we want differences ≡ 0 mod K).

freq-counter.387: First unique char. Counter pass over s; second pass returns first idx where count[s[i]]==1.
freq-counter.169: Majority element. Counter works O(n) space; Boyer-Moore voting is the optimal O(1) — same conceptual frequency-tracking, just collapsed to two vars.
freq-counter.49: Group anagrams. Counter form: 26-int tuple as group key. Beats sort-key when k (word length) is large.
freq-counter.242: Valid anagram. Compare two 26-counters; or single counter with += and -=, check all zero.
freq-counter.567: Permutation in string. Sliding window of len(s1) over s2; track 'matched chars' so the window-check is O(1) per slide.
freq-counter.229: Majority Element II (> n/3). Boyer-Moore generalised to 2 candidates + final verification pass.
freq-counter.350: Intersection 2 arrays II (with multiplicity). Counter on smaller array; iterate larger, decrement and emit on hit.
freq-counter.819: Most common word (excluding banned). Tokenise, lowercase, strip punct; counter over words ∖ banned; argmax.
freq-counter.1153: String transforms into another. Mapping s[i]→t[i] must be a function (single-valued). If s==t trivial; else need an unused 27th char (≤25 distinct in t) for the temporary cycle break.
freq-counter.1657: Determine if two strings are close. Op1+Op2 preserve: (a) SET of chars must match exactly, (b) SORTED freq multiset must match.
freq-counter.266: Palindrome permutation. Counter; ≤ 1 char with odd count.
freq-counter.1481: Least unique ints after K removals. Counter, sort COUNTS ascending, greedily consume smallest-count keys with budget K.
freq-counter.734: Sentence similarity. Word-pair set (both directions); walk word-by-word, check membership.

seen-set.217: Contains duplicate. One pass; add to set; on first re-encounter return true.
seen-set.219: Contains duplicate within K indices. Sliding-window set of size K+1: add cur, evict at i-K, check membership before add.
seen-set.287: Find duplicate. Seen-set is O(n) space — works but Floyd's tortoise/hare (tp-fast-slow tag) gives O(1) space — that's the optimal.
seen-set.141: Linked List cycle. Seen-set O(n) space — Floyd's two-pointer (tp-fast-slow tag) is O(1) optimal. Both tagged so the comparison is visible.
seen-set.1488: Avoid flood. Map lake→last-rain-day; sorted set of dry days; on rain to a wet lake, bisect for the next dry day to drain. (Hash + binary-search combo — could warrant a sub-micro.)
seen-set.1452: People whose list contains all of another. For each list build set; outer loop, subset-check via .issubset / all-in.

dp-1d-linear.338: Counting bits. dp[i] = dp[i>>1] + (i&1) (or dp[i & (i-1)] + 1). Reads a NON-adjacent earlier index → full table retained, cannot roll to O(1). The canonical contrast to rolling-state-fixed-window.

rolling-state-fixed-window.509: Fibonacci. dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Window width 2 → keep two scalars (a, b = b, a+b). O(1) space, never allocate the table.
rolling-state-fixed-window.70: Climbing stairs. dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]. Same 2-wide window as Fib; answer is a count of ways.
rolling-state-fixed-window.198: House robber. dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + a[i]). Two rolling vars; only the last two states matter.
rolling-state-fixed-window.213: House robber II (circular). Two linear passes over [0..n-2] and [1..n-1]; each pass is the same 2-wide rolling window, take the max.
rolling-state-fixed-window.91: Decode ways. dp[i] = dp[i-1] (if s[i-1]≠'0') + dp[i-2] (if s[i-2..i-1] ∈ 10..26). Fixed 2-back window despite the validity guards.
rolling-state-fixed-window.746: Min cost climbing stairs. dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]). 2-wide window.
rolling-state-fixed-window.1137: Tribonacci. dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2] + dp[i-3]. Window width 3 → three rolling scalars; still O(1) space.

rolling-state-variable-window.837: New 21 Game. dp[i] = (dp[i+1] + … + dp[i+W]) / W (prob of stopping < K). Window width W is a runtime parameter; keep ONE running sum, slide it (window += dp[i] − dp[i+W]) → O(n) not O(n·W).

augmented-state-reachability.403: Frog jump. State = (stone, speed). reach[stone] = set of arrival speeds; from each speed v branch to v-1,v,v+1 and land if the target stone exists. Goal reachable iff reach[last] is non-empty. Each node holds a SET of states → no scalar roll.

ordered-interval-merge.352: Data Stream as Disjoint Intervals. Keep intervals in an ordered map start→end. On addNum(v): skip if already covered; locate the floor/ceil neighbours by binary search; merge if v touches the left (end+1==v) and/or right (v+1==start) interval, erasing absorbed ones. getIntervals returns entries in key order. O(log n) per add.

dfs-memo.329: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix. dfs(r,c) = longest strictly-increasing run starting at (r,c); cache it. The grid is an implicit DAG (edges to larger neighbours), so memoized DFS = top-down DP = DAG longest path. O(R·C). Also tagged topo-sort::dag-critical-path and DS matrices + graph.

dfs-template.200: Number of Islands. For each unvisited '1', DFS (mark to '0' or visited set), ++count. Same as dfs-grid-flood — listed under both pre-prune.
dfs-template.695: Max area of island. DFS RETURNS subtree-area (1 + sum of 4 neighbour calls); track global max.
dfs-template.547: Number of provinces. For each unvisited city, DFS via adjacency matrix marking; ++count.
dfs-template.133: Clone graph. Map<orig, clone>; on visit, create clone, recurse to each neighbour, attach. Pure visited-via-map idiom.
dfs-template.417: Pacific Atlantic. Two DFSes from boundary cells (reverse: water flows DOWN-to-UP); mark cells reachable to each ocean; intersect the two boolean grids.
dfs-template.841: Keys and Rooms. DFS from room 0; visited[i]=true; recurse into each key in rooms[i]. Check all visited.
dfs-template.489: Robot Room Cleaner. DFS with MOTION backtracking — for each of 4 directions: clean, move, recurse, move-back, turn. Distinct shape worth own sub-micro if it grows.
dfs-template.1192: Critical Connections (Tarjan). disc[]/low[] arrays; back-edges update low. Bridge when low[v] > disc[u]. (Tarjan deserves its own micro; tracked for future.)
dfs-template.582: Kill Process. Build child-list adjacency; DFS from killPid collecting all descendants.
dfs-template.1376: Time to inform all employees. Build manager→reports adjacency; DFS from head returning max-path-time over subtrees; combine with informTime[u].
dfs-template.1530: Number of good leaf pairs. DFS returns LIST of leaf-distances from current root; for each ancestor, count pairs across left+right with sum ≤ distance.

tp-converging.344: Reverse String. l=0, r=n-1; swap and shrink. O(n/2) ops, O(1) space.
tp-converging.345: Reverse Vowels. Same shape, but skip non-vowels on each side before swapping; only swap when both pointers land on vowels.
tp-converging.977: Squares of Sorted Array. Sorted with possible negatives. Compare |arr[l]| vs |arr[r]|; place larger² at result[end], advance the matching side, decrement end.
tp-converging.925: Long Pressed Name. Two pointers (i on name, j on typed). If chars match advance both; else allow advance j only if typed[j]==typed[j-1] (i.e. long-press repeat). At end, i must equal name.length.
tp-converging.161: One Edit Distance. Walk both strings in parallel; on first mismatch, try one of (replace, insert into shorter, delete from longer) and check rest matches.
tp-converging.243: Shortest Word Distance. Single pass; track lastIdx of word1 and word2; on each hit update min |i - other.lastIdx|.
tp-converging.360: Sort Transformed Array. f(x)=ax²+bx+c is convex (a>0) or concave (a<0). Use 2-ptr from ends; pick the extreme f(l) vs f(r), append, advance.
tp-converging.415: Add Strings. Walk both strings from RIGHT; track carry; prepend each digit-sum % 10; flush carry.
tp-converging.67: Add Binary. Same right-to-left two-pointer + carry, base-2 instead of 10.

dp-2-strings.72: Edit Distance. dp[i][j] = if s1[i-1]==s2[j-1] then dp[i-1][j-1] else 1 + min(insert dp[i][j-1], delete dp[i-1][j], replace dp[i-1][j-1]).
dp-2-strings.583: Delete Operation for 2 Strings. answer = m + n - 2 * LCS(s1, s2). Reduces to 1143.
dp-2-strings.1143: LCS. dp[i][j] = if match dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]). Workhorse 2D DP.
dp-2-strings.10: Regex Matching. dp[i][j] for s[0..i] vs p[0..j]. '*' = zero-or-more of prev char: dp[i][j-2] (zero) OR (dp[i-1][j] if prev matches s[i-1]).
dp-2-strings.44: Wildcard Matching. '*' matches zero-or-more ANY chars: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] OR dp[i][j-1]. '?' matches one. Simpler than #10 because '*' isn't tied to prev char.
dp-2-strings.97: Interleaving String. dp[i][j] = can s3[0..i+j] be formed by interleaving s1[0..i] and s2[0..j]? Transition uses s3[i+j-1] matching s1[i-1] OR s2[j-1].
dp-2-strings.115: Distinct Subsequences. dp[i][j] = #ways s[0..i] can form t[0..j]. If match: dp[i-1][j-1] + dp[i-1][j] (use or skip s[i-1]); else dp[i-1][j].
dp-2-strings.727: Min Window Subsequence. dp[i][j] = the START INDEX in S of the smallest window ENDING at S[i] that contains T[0..j]. On match propagate dp[i-1][j-1]; else carry dp[i-1][j].

bfs-shortest-unweighted.127: Word Ladder. BFS over implicit graph (transform 1 char at a time); enqueue 1-step neighbours; return depth when target popped. Bidirectional BFS halves the search (separate sub-micro bfs-bidirectional).
bfs-shortest-unweighted.752: Open the Lock. BFS over 4-digit states; 8 neighbours each (±1 each wheel); skip deadends set; first reach target.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1091: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix. 8-direction BFS from (0,0) over '0' cells; dist = cells visited. First time you pop (n-1, n-1) is the answer.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.433: Min Genetic Mutation. Word-ladder shape but mutation alphabet is {A,C,G,T}. Bank as the visited set.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1730: Shortest Path to Get Food. BFS from '*' over '.' cells; the first '#' (food) popped is the answer.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.815: Bus Routes. BFS over (stop, routes-taken). For each stop, enqueue ALL stops of every route serving it; visited set keys on ROUTES not stops to avoid re-traversing same route.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1197: Min Knight Moves. 8 L-shaped neighbours; (x,y) symmetry means you only need to explore the first octant (use |x|, |y|).
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1284: Min Flips Convert Binary Matrix. Encode matrix as INTEGER (bit per cell); 12 (3x3 max) cells = 2^9 states. Each move XORs a 5-bit mask. BFS over int states; visited set of ints.
bfs-shortest-unweighted.1293: Shortest Path Obstacles Elim. BFS over (row, col, k-erasures-used). State-space BFS — k is the EXTRA dimension. First time (m-1, n-1, *) popped is answer.

monotonic-stack.496: Next Greater Element I. Monotonic decreasing stack on nums2; for each cur, pop while stack-top < cur and store nextGreater[popped] = cur; then look up nums1 in the resulting map.
monotonic-stack.503: Next Greater II (circular). Walk indices i in 0..2n-1, use i % n; same monotonic decreasing stack; only assign answer on FIRST pass through each index.
monotonic-stack.739: Daily Temperatures. Monotonic decreasing stack of INDICES; on each new temp, pop while stack-top temp < cur and set answer[popped] = i - popped.
monotonic-stack.901: Online Stock Span. Monotonic decreasing stack of (price, span). On new price, pop and sum spans while top.price ≤ cur; push (cur, sumSpans + 1).
monotonic-stack.1019: Next Greater Node in Linked List. Materialise to array (one pass) then standard daily-temperatures monotonic stack. Linked-list specific because a single forward walk can't see future.

subset-combination.78: Subsets (no dupes). Backtrack(i): emit path; for j in [i..n): pick a[j], recurse(j+1), un-pick. Iterative bitmask variant: for mask in 0..2^n.
subset-combination.90: Subsets II (with dupes). Sort first. At each depth, skip a[j] if a[j]==a[j-1] AND j>i (avoid emitting the SAME subset twice at the same depth).
subset-combination.39: Combination Sum (each candidate reusable). Same template, but recurse(j) NOT recurse(j+1) — allows re-picking the same element. Prune when sum > target.
subset-combination.40: Combination Sum II (each used once + dupes). Sort + recurse(j+1) + skip-dup-at-same-depth (same trick as #90).
subset-combination.216: Combination Sum III (use digits 1..9, exactly k numbers, sum n). Backtrack with start index 1..9, depth ≤ k, prune if sum > n or remaining can't reach.
subset-combination.491: Increasing Subsequences. Backtrack; only pick if >= last picked; depth-local 'seen values' set to dedupe (can't sort first because we'd lose original order).
subset-combination.77: Combinations (k from n). Backtrack(start, path): if len==k emit; for j in [start..n]: include j, recurse(j+1), exclude.

kadane.53: Max Subarray. cur = max(x, cur + x); best = max(best, cur). Single pass O(n).
kadane.152: Max Product Subarray. Track BOTH cur_max and cur_min (negative × negative flips sign). cur_max' = max(x, x·cur_max, x·cur_min); cur_min similarly.
kadane.918: Max Sum Circular Subarray. Two answers: (a) standard kadane non-wrap; (b) wrap = total − minSubarray. Answer = max(a, b). Edge: all-negative → answer = a (b would be 0).
kadane.1567: Max Length Positive-Product Subarray. Track lengths of (current positive run, current negative run). Walk; reset on zero; swap pos/neg on negative element.

floyd-cycle.141: Linked List Cycle. slow=head, fast=head; both step (slow 1, fast 2). If they ever meet, cycle exists. O(1) extra space.
floyd-cycle.142: Linked List Cycle II — find cycle START. After meeting, reset slow to head; both step 1; they meet at cycle start. Math: distance head→start = distance meeting→start (mod cycle len).
floyd-cycle.287: Find Duplicate Number. Treat nums as a linked list — nums[i] is the 'next' pointer. Cycle MUST exist because some value repeats. Cycle start = the duplicate.
floyd-cycle.202: Happy Number. Treat digit-square-sum sequence as implicit list. Floyd detects cycle; if cycle reaches 1, happy; else unhappy.

bracket-match.20: Valid Parentheses. Push openers; on closer, top must match else fail. Empty stack at end ⇒ valid.
bracket-match.32: Longest Valid Parentheses. Stack of INDICES with −1 sentinel for 'last invalid before'. On '(' push i; on ')' pop; if stack empty push i as new sentinel; else max(answer, i − top).
bracket-match.921: Min Add to Make Parens Valid. Two counters: openNeeded, closeUnmatched. Single pass. Answer = sum at end.
bracket-match.1249: Min Remove to Make Valid. Pass 1: stack of '(' indices; pop on each ')'; leftover stack = '(' to remove; also collect unmatched ')'. Pass 2: build result skipping marked indices.

monotonic-deque.239: Sliding Window Maximum. Deque of INDICES, monotonic decreasing on values. For each i: pop front if i − k ≥ front; pop back while nums[back] < nums[i]; push i. Front is window max.
monotonic-deque.1438: Longest Subarray Abs Diff ≤ Limit. TWO deques — one max-decreasing, one min-increasing. For each r expand; while (max − min) > limit, shrink l updating both deques.
monotonic-deque.862: Shortest Subarray Sum ≥ K. Prefix sums; monotonic INCREASING deque of indices. For each i: while pre[i] − pre[front] ≥ K, pop front and update answer; while pre[back] ≥ pre[i], pop back (later prefix is better); push i.
monotonic-deque.918: Max Sum Circular Subarray. Alternative deque approach using prefix sums; standard solve is kadane-twice (see kadane note). Listed here for the deque option.
monotonic-deque.1696: Jump Game VI. dp[i] = nums[i] + max(dp[i−k..i−1]). Monotonic decreasing deque of dp values to get O(1) max-lookup over the sliding K window.

index-as-hash.41: First Missing Positive. Place each nums[i] at index nums[i]−1 via swapping (while in [1..n] and not already correct). Then find first i where nums[i] != i+1 ⇒ answer = i+1.
index-as-hash.268: Missing Number. Many ways: index-as-hash via swap-to-correct-slot; XOR (xor all + 0..n); or sum-formula (n(n+1)/2 − sum). All O(n) / O(1).
index-as-hash.287: Find Duplicate Number. Sign-flip variant: for each x, flip sign of nums[abs(x)−1]; if already negative, x is the duplicate. (Floyd's cycle is the other O(1)-space approach.)
index-as-hash.442: Find All Duplicates. Sign-flip: for each x, flip nums[abs(x)−1]; if already negative, append abs(x) to answer.
index-as-hash.448: Find All Disappeared Numbers. Sign-flip pass; indices STILL POSITIVE at end correspond to missing numbers (i+1).

bs-textbook.34: Find First and Last Position. Two binary searches — lower_bound (first ≥ target) and upper_bound (first > target). If lower_bound's value != target return [-1,-1].
bs-textbook.35: Search Insert Position. Plain lower_bound — return l at end (works whether target found or insertion point).
bs-textbook.704: Binary Search. Textbook l ≤ r loop; mid = l + (r-l)/2 to avoid overflow.
bs-textbook.278: First Bad Version. lower_bound on the bad-flag predicate; bad() is the monotone API.
bs-textbook.744: Smallest Letter Greater Than Target. upper_bound on chars; if past end, wrap to letters[0].
bs-textbook.540: Single Element in Sorted Array. Pairs at even indices; check if pair starting at mid (rounded down to even) is intact — if a[mid]==a[mid+1], single is to the right; else left.
bs-textbook.374: Guess Number Higher or Lower. Textbook BS using guess() API as the comparator.
bs-textbook.275: H-Index II (sorted). Find smallest i where citations[i] ≥ n − i. Answer = n − i.
bs-textbook.222: Count Complete Tree Nodes. Per subtree: compare full-left vs full-right depths; if equal, perfect subtree = 2^h − 1; else recurse both. Binary-search on last-level index gives O(log² n).
bs-textbook.436: Find Right Interval. Sort intervals by START with original index; for each interval's END, lower_bound to find first start ≥ end.
bs-textbook.74: Search a 2D Matrix. Treat as 1D flattened sorted array; mid → (mid/n, mid%n). O(log(m·n)).
bs-textbook.240: Search a 2D Matrix II. Rows+cols sorted but NOT globally — staircase from top-right (or bottom-left): on > target go left/down; on < go right/up. O(m+n).
bs-textbook.1351: Count Negatives Sorted Matrix. Each row sorted descending; per row, binary-search for first negative; accumulate (n − idx). Alternative: staircase like 240, O(m+n).

bs-on-answer.875: Koko Eating Bananas. Find min speed K such that totalHours(K) ≤ H. lo=1, hi=max(piles); feasibility is monotone in K.
bs-on-answer.1011: Capacity to Ship Packages in D Days. Find min capacity C s.t. shipsNeeded(C) ≤ D. lo=max(weights), hi=sum(weights).
bs-on-answer.410: Split Array Largest Sum. Find min largest-sum across K splits. lo=max(arr), hi=sum.
bs-on-answer.1482: Min Days to Make M Bouquets. Find min day d s.t. canMakeBouquets(d) ≥ m. Feasibility: scan and count contiguous runs ≥ k.
bs-on-answer.2141: Max Running Time of N Computers. Find max time t s.t. all n computers can run for t (sum of min(battery, t) across all ≥ n·t).
bs-on-answer.1898: Max Removable Chars Still Subseq. Find max k s.t. removing first k indices still leaves p as a subseq of s. Two-pointer check is the feasibility predicate.
bs-on-answer.2616: Min Max Diff via K Pairs. Find min threshold t s.t. we can form k disjoint pairs with |diff| ≤ t. Sort, greedy-pair adjacent.
bs-on-answer.2517: Max Tastiness of K-Candy Basket. Find max gap g s.t. we can pick k items with pairwise diff ≥ g. Sort + greedy feasibility.
bs-on-answer.719: K-th Smallest Pair Distance. Binary-search on distance value; countPairs(d) ≤ d uses sliding window after sort.
bs-on-answer.1648: Sell Diminishing-Valued Balls. Find max base sell-count k s.t. total balls sold (using floor-and-leftover) ≥ orders.

dfs-tree-orders.144: BT Preorder. visit, recurse left, recurse right. Iterative: stack of nodes; pop, visit, push right then left so left pops first.
dfs-tree-orders.94: BT Inorder. recurse left, visit, recurse right. Iterative: go-left pushing each, pop visit, then recurse right.
dfs-tree-orders.145: BT Postorder. recurse left, recurse right, visit. Iterative: easiest is modified preorder (root → right → left) collected in reverse.
dfs-tree-orders.543: Diameter. Post-order — return height (1 + max children); update global with leftHeight + rightHeight at current node.
dfs-tree-orders.124: BT Max Path Sum. Post-order — return max single-side gain CLAMPED to 0 (don't take negative subtrees); update global with leftGain + rightGain + node.val.

post-order-depth.104: Max Depth. 1 + max(leftDepth, rightDepth). Base null = 0.
post-order-depth.543: Diameter. At each node, candidate = leftDepth + rightDepth; return 1 + max(left, right) upward.
post-order-depth.110: Balanced Tree. Return height OR sentinel −1 if any subtree unbalanced. Propagate −1 upward to short-circuit.
post-order-depth.687: Longest Univalue Path. Per node return univalue-path-length downward; if child.val == node.val, length includes child; combine left + right at the node for the global max.
post-order-depth.1245: Tree Diameter (general N-ary graph). Same shape but n-ary; track TOP-2 child depths for diameter; or 2-BFS sweep.
post-order-depth.124: BT Max Path Sum. Return max single-side gain (clamped to 0); update global with left + right + val.
post-order-depth.222: Count Complete Tree Nodes. Hybrid post-order + binary-search: compare leftmost vs rightmost path lengths; if equal, perfect = 2^h − 1; else recurse both. O(log² n).

kahn-bfs.207: Course Schedule. Can-finish = Kahn processes all N courses (no leftover ⇒ no cycle).
kahn-bfs.210: Course Schedule II. Return the Kahn order; [] if a cycle remains. Use a min-heap for the lexicographically smallest order.
kahn-bfs.269: Alien Dictionary. Build edges from the first differing char of adjacent words, then Kahn for the letter order; a prefix-after-longer-word or a cycle ⇒ invalid.
kahn-bfs.444: Sequence Reconstruction. The order is UNIQUE iff at every Kahn step the queue holds exactly one node.
kahn-bfs.10004: Privilege Resolution. Topological order over the privilege-dependency DAG.
kahn-bfs.10012: Schedule prerequisite classes with retakes. Kahn; on a failed/retaken course push it back onto the queue and re-run.

dfs-cycle-detect.802: Find Eventual Safe States. A node is safe iff it reaches no cycle — 3-color DFS (or Kahn on the reversed graph).
dfs-cycle-detect.1059: All Paths Source→Dest. Valid iff no reachable cycle and every terminal node is the destination — 3-color DFS.
dfs-cycle-detect.10026: Implement DFS (recursive + iterative) with cycle detection + topo order. Reverse of finishing order = a topological order.

dag-critical-path.329: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix. DFS-memo on the implicit DAG (edges to strictly larger neighbours); answer = max path length.
dag-critical-path.1857: Largest Color Value in a Directed Graph. Topo DP of per-color counts along paths; a cycle ⇒ -1.
dag-critical-path.2050: Parallel Courses III. finish[v] = time[v] + max(finish[pred]); answer = max(finish). Each course starts when ITS prereqs finish (not a barrier).
dag-critical-path.2127: Maximum Employees to Be Invited. Functional graph: longest chains feeding 2-cycles, plus the largest pure cycle.
dag-critical-path.10019: Compute total time to finish all courses (per-task duration). Earliest-finish topo DP.
dag-critical-path.10045: Course Completion Time. Same earliest-finish topo DP; answer = max finish.

layered-waves.1136: Parallel Courses. Min semesters = number of Kahn waves (= longest dependency chain).
layered-waves.10025: Schedule dependent services with layered startup. Each wave starts only after the entire previous wave is up.

leaf-peeling.310: Minimum Height Trees. Trim all degree-1 leaves layer by layer; the last 1 or 2 nodes remaining are the MHT roots.

lp-dag.1857: Largest Color Value in a Directed Graph. Topo-order DP of per-color path counts; cycle ⇒ -1.
lp-dag.2050: Parallel Courses III. finish[v] = time[v] + max(finish[pred]); answer = max(finish) = critical path.
lp-dag.2127: Maximum Employees to Be Invited. Functional graph: longest chains feeding 2-cycles + largest cycle.
lp-dag.10019: Compute total time to finish all courses. Earliest-finish topo DP = longest weighted path.
lp-dag.10045: Course Completion Time. Same critical-path DP; answer = max finish.

lp-grid.329: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix. Grid is an implicit DAG (edges to strictly larger cells); memoize the longest run from each cell. = lp-dag specialised to a grid; also dfs::dfs-memo + topo-sort::dag-critical-path. O(R·C).

lp-tree.124: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum. Post-order: each node returns max downward sum; update best with node + left + right (clamp negatives to 0).
lp-tree.543: Diameter of Binary Tree. Post-order depths; best = max(L + R) edges through each node.
lp-tree.687: Longest Univalue Path. Like diameter but only extend through equal-value children.
lp-tree.1245: Tree Diameter (general tree). Two BFS/DFS, or one post-order combining the top two child depths.
lp-tree.1372: Longest ZigZag Path. Post-order returning (left-extend, right-extend); alternate direction each step.
lp-tree.1522: Diameter of N-Ary Tree. Post-order; combine the top TWO child depths among all children.

topo-sort.207: Course Schedule — can you finish? Kahn: queue of in-deg 0; decrement neighbours' in-deg; if final processed count == n, yes. Alternative: DFS 3-color cycle detect.
topo-sort.210: Course Schedule II — output order. Same Kahn; record pop order. Result is the topological ordering (any valid one).
topo-sort.269: Alien Dictionary. Build chars + edges from adjacent word pairs (first mismatch ⇒ a < b). Edge case: word1 is prefix of word2 with len1 > len2 ⇒ invalid. Then topo-sort.
topo-sort.444: Sequence Reconstruction. Kahn + UNIQUENESS check: at each step, EXACTLY ONE in-deg-0 node remains AND it matches the expected next of the original sequence.
topo-sort.802: Find Eventual Safe States. Reverse the graph; topo from out-deg-0 originals (sinks). Safe = nodes reaching a sink only.
topo-sort.2050: Parallel Courses III. Topo + DP — for each course, finishTime = max(prereqFinishes) + duration. Tracking max over a DAG.
topo-sort.1857: Largest Color Value in DAG. Topo + DP — count[v][color] = max over incoming neighbours; add 1 for v's own color.
topo-sort.1136: Parallel Courses. Topo by LEVELS (Kahn drains entire in-deg-0 batch per round); answer = number of rounds; −1 if cycle.

dp-2d-grid.62: Unique Paths. dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1]. Base dp[0][*]=1, dp[*][0]=1. Rolling 1D row works for O(n) space.
dp-2d-grid.63: Unique Paths II (obstacles). Same recurrence; if grid[r][c]==1 set dp[r][c]=0 (obstacle blocks the path).
dp-2d-grid.64: Min Path Sum. dp[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(dp[r-1][c], dp[r][c-1]). Edges have a single inbound direction.
dp-2d-grid.174: Dungeon Game. REVERSE direction — fill from bottom-right backward. dp[r][c] = max(1, min(dp[r+1][c], dp[r][c+1]) − grid[r][c]). Forward DP fails because future damage matters.
dp-2d-grid.931: Min Falling Path Sum. dp[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(dp[r-1][c-1], dp[r-1][c], dp[r-1][c+1]). Skip out-of-bound diagonals at edges.
dp-2d-grid.120: Triangle (bottom-up). dp[c] = triangle[r][c] + min(dp[c], dp[c+1]) sweeping r from bottom-1 → 0. One-array rolling, O(n) space.

dp-grid-two-pass.542: 01 Matrix. dp[r][c] = distance to nearest 0. Init 0-cells to 0, others to INF. Pass 1 (top-left→bottom-right) relaxes against up+left (+1); pass 2 (bottom-right→top-left) relaxes against down+right (+1). Two sweeps cover all 4 directions. O(m·n). Same result as multi-source BFS, written as a DP.

prefix-sum-hashmap.560: Subarray Sum K. Map[prefix] = count of prior occurrences. For each new prefix, answer += map.get(prefix − K, 0); then ++map[prefix]. Handles negatives (sliding window can't).
prefix-sum-hashmap.974: Subarray Sums Divisible by K. Map[prefix mod K] = count. Same engine, but key on residue. Normalise negative mods via ((mod + K) % K).
prefix-sum-hashmap.525: Contiguous Array (equal 0s and 1s). Treat 0 as −1; problem becomes 'longest subarray summing to 0' → Map[prefix] = FIRST index seen; on re-encounter update max length.
prefix-sum-hashmap.523: Continuous Subarray Sum (length ≥ 2, sum % K == 0). Map[prefix mod K] = first index. If two prefixes share mod AND |idx diff| ≥ 2, found.
prefix-sum-hashmap.304: Range Sum Query 2D (immutable). Build 2D prefix sum via inclusion-exclusion: pre[r][c] = pre[r-1][c] + pre[r][c-1] − pre[r-1][c-1] + mat[r-1][c-1]. Query is O(1).
prefix-sum-hashmap.363: Max Sum Rectangle ≤ K. For each pair of cols (l, r), compute row sums between them; treat as 1D 'max subarray sum ≤ K' via TreeSet of prefixes — for each prefix, find ceiling(prefix − K).

lca-dfs.236: LCA of Binary Tree. def f(n): if !n || n==p || n==q: return n; l=f(n.left); r=f(n.right); if both: return n; else l || r. The first node where the recursion has matches from BOTH sides IS the LCA.
lca-dfs.235: LCA of BST. Walk from root: if p,q both < node go left; both > go right; else (split or hit) return node. O(h), no recursion needed.
lca-dfs.1644: LCA of BT II (nodes might NOT exist). Track found-flags as out-params; return non-null only if BOTH found.
lca-dfs.1650: LCA of BT III (each node has parent pointer). Two-pointer alignment trick: walk both UP; on null restart at the other start; they meet at LCA. O(h) space-free.
lca-dfs.1123: LCA of Deepest Leaves. Post-order returning (depth, lca); combine left/right at each node: if depths equal lca=node, else carry the deeper side.
lca-dfs.1676: LCA of BT IV (k nodes). Generalisation of #236 — same recursion but checking against a SET of targets; return current node if its subtree contains all targets.

top-k.215: Kth Largest in Array. Min-heap of size K — push each, pop if size > K; final top = K-th largest. Quickselect is O(n) average alternative.
top-k.347: Top K Frequent. Counter → min-heap of size K keyed on freq. OR bucket sort by freq (O(n)) when frequencies fit a small range.
top-k.692: Top K Frequent Words. Min-heap of (freq, word) with custom comparator: freq asc, word DESC (so the lexicographically larger word pops out when freq ties).
top-k.973: K Closest Points to Origin. Max-heap of size K keyed on dist² (so the FARTHEST pops on overflow). Quickselect alternative.
top-k.703: Kth Largest in Stream. Min-heap of size K maintained across add() calls; top = current K-th largest. O(log K) per add.
top-k.1337: K Weakest Rows. Per row count soldiers (or BS for first 0); min-heap of (count, rowIdx) trimmed to K. Or partial sort.

palindrome-two-ptr.125: Valid Palindrome. l=0, r=n-1; skip non-alphanumeric on each side; lowercase compare; advance.
palindrome-two-ptr.680: Valid Palindrome II (allow one delete). Walk converging; on first mismatch try EITHER skip-left or skip-right and verify rest. At most one delete allowed.
palindrome-two-ptr.234: Palindrome Linked List. O(1) space: find middle (slow/fast), reverse second half, compare first vs reversed-second. Restoring the list is optional.

iterative-reverse.206: Reverse Linked List. 3 pointers (prev=null, cur=head, next): while cur: next=cur.next; cur.next=prev; prev=cur; cur=next. Return prev.
iterative-reverse.92: Reverse LL II (positions m..n). Walk to m-1; reverse the next (n-m+1) nodes using the 3-ptr template; splice back to the surrounding tail.
iterative-reverse.25: Reverse Nodes in K-Group. Check K nodes ahead; if K available reverse them via the template, then recurse/iterate on the rest. Leftover < K typically left alone.
iterative-reverse.234: Palindrome LL (uses iterative-reverse). After finding middle (slow/fast), apply the 3-ptr template to second half, then compare with first half.
iterative-reverse.24: Swap Nodes in Pairs. Special case of K-group with K=2 — or write a small dedicated 4-ptr swap (dummy → first → second → swap → advance).

two-sum-hash.1: Two Sum unsorted — one-pass hash, store seen→idx, check (target − x) before insert.
two-sum-hash.167: Two Sum sorted. Hash works but converging 2-ptr is optimal (O(1) space). Tag kept for the universal complement-lookup angle.
two-sum-hash.653: Two Sum BST. Inorder collect + complement OR two converging iterators (forward + reverse inorder).

in-place-read-write.26: Remove Duplicates Sorted. write=1; for read 1..n: if a[read]!=a[read-1] then a[write++]=a[read].
in-place-read-write.27: Remove Element. write=0; for read 0..n: if a[read]!=val then a[write++]=a[read].
in-place-read-write.80: Remove Dup Sorted II (≤2). write tracks position; copy if write<2 OR a[read]!=a[write-2].
in-place-read-write.283: Move Zeroes. write=0; for read: if a[read]!=0 copy; finally pad with zeros (or swap as you go).
in-place-read-write.75: Sort Colors. Dutch National Flag: 3 pointers (lo, mid, hi); on 0 swap mid↔lo and ++both; on 1 ++mid; on 2 swap mid↔hi and --hi.
in-place-read-write.228: Summary Ranges. Walk; when a[i]!=a[i-1]+1 close current range, start new. Single-pass O(n).
in-place-read-write.163: Missing Ranges. The read-sweep of #228 emitting the GAPS instead of the runs — compare each element to prev+1 and close a range when they differ. Nothing is written back into the input.
in-place-read-write.362: Design Hit Counter. The write is circular: bucket = t % 300, and a stale bucket is overwritten rather than cleared. In-place reuse of a fixed buffer, not compaction.
in-place-read-write.484: Find Permutation. Build 1..n, then reverse each maximal 'D' run in place — the write is a segment reversal rather than a per-element copy.
in-place-read-write.624: Maximum Distance in Arrays. One sweep carrying the best min/max so far. Read-pointer only, nothing written back — the loosest fit on this card.

rotate-reverse.189: Rotate Array by K. Reverse(0,n); reverse(0,K); reverse(K,n). O(n) time, O(1) space.
rotate-reverse.48: Rotate Image 90°. Transpose (swap a[i][j]↔a[j][i]) then reverse each row.
rotate-reverse.151: Reverse Words. Reverse whole string; then reverse each word in place. (Or trim + split + reverse list.)

anagram-keying.242: Valid Anagram. Counter == counter; or 26-count array; or sorted-string compare.
anagram-keying.49: Group Anagrams. Map<sorted-string-or-count-tuple, list>. Count-tuple beats sort-string when k (length) is large.
anagram-keying.438: Find All Anagrams. Sliding window of len(p) over s; compare window-counter to p-counter via 'matched chars' trick for O(1) slide.
anagram-keying.273: Integer to English. Tokenise into thousand-chunks; map digit-position → word. (Note: 'anagram-keying' is a stretch — it's just chunked mapping; could need own micro.)

expand-around-center.5: Longest Palindromic Substring. For each center i (and i,i+1), expand l--,r++ while s[l]==s[r]; track longest.
expand-around-center.647: Palindromic Substrings count. Same expand-around-center, count each successful expansion as one palindrome.
expand-around-center.1312: Min Insertions to Make Palindrome. dp[l][r] OR LCS(s, reverse(s)) — answer = n − LCS. Expand isn't the optimal here; usually DP.

minimum-window.76: Min Window Substring. Need-counter + matched-count; expand r; while matched==|need| shrink l updating min window.
minimum-window.567: Permutation in String. Fixed window of len(s1); sliding compare via matched-count.
minimum-window.438: Find Anagrams. Same fixed-window sliding-anagram trick as 567; collect start indices.
minimum-window.30: Substring with Concat of All Words. Window aligned at each offset 0..wordLen-1; words as units; counter-match per window slide.

word-ladder-bfs.127: Word Ladder. BFS over implicit graph (transform 1 char at a time); shortest hop count.
word-ladder-bfs.433: Min Genetic Mutation. Same shape; ACGT mutation alphabet; bank as valid-set / visited.
word-ladder-bfs.752: Open the Lock. 4-digit state space; ±1 each wheel; BFS until target; skip deadends.
word-ladder-bfs.126: Word Ladder II (all shortest paths). BFS to build layer-by-layer parent-map; then DFS/backtrack from end to start collecting paths.

edit-distance-dp.72: Edit Distance. dp[i][j] = match ? dp[i-1][j-1] : 1 + min(insert, delete, replace).
edit-distance-dp.1143: LCS. dp[i][j] = match ? dp[i-1][j-1]+1 : max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
edit-distance-dp.10: Regex Match. '*' = zero+ of prev char; dp[i][j-2] OR (dp[i-1][j] if prev matches s[i-1]).
edit-distance-dp.44: Wildcard Match. '*' = zero+ of ANY; dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] OR dp[i][j-1].
edit-distance-dp.97: Interleaving String. dp[i][j]: can s3[0..i+j] be formed? Transition uses s3[i+j-1] matching s1 or s2.

string-match-kmp.28: Implement strStr. Build LPS of needle; scan haystack with fall-back on mismatch. O(n+m).
string-match-kmp.459: Repeated Substring Pattern. LPS[n-1] gives largest proper-prefix-suffix; valid iff n % (n - lps[n-1]) == 0.
string-match-kmp.214: Shortest Palindrome. Build LPS of (s + '#' + reverse(s)); lps[last] = longest palindrome prefix of s; prepend reverse of the rest.
string-match-kmp.686: Repeated String Match. Append A until len ≥ len(B); then strStr (KMP) to check.
string-match-kmp.1392: Longest Happy Prefix. LPS[n-1] of the string IS the answer (longest proper prefix that's also a suffix).
string-match-kmp.1408: String Matching in Array. KMP each pair, or just .contains() — KMP overkill for tiny strings.

rolling-hash.1044: Longest Duplicate Substring. Binary-search the length L; for each L roll a hash over all length-L windows into a set — a matching (verified) hash means L is feasible. O(n log n).
rolling-hash.187: Repeated DNA Sequences. Fixed length 10 — rolling hash (or direct seen-set) to flag substrings seen more than once.
rolling-hash.28: strStr via Rabin-Karp: hash the pattern, roll over the text, verify on hash match. O(n+m) average — the hashing alternative to KMP.
rolling-hash.1408: String Matching in an Array. Hash each word and test substring containment via rolling hash (KMP is the deterministic alternative).

slow-fast-middle.876: Middle of LL. slow=head, fast=head; while fast && fast.next: slow=slow.next, fast=fast.next.next. On even, returns the SECOND middle.
slow-fast-middle.234: Palindrome LL — find middle first, then reverse second half, then compare.
slow-fast-middle.143: Reorder List. Find middle; reverse second half; merge first + reversed-second interleaved.

nth-from-end.19: Remove N-th From End. fast advances N first; then both advance until fast hits null; slow points to the node BEFORE target. Use dummy head for clean splice.

aligned-intersect.160: LL Intersection. a, b = headA, headB; loop a = a ? a.next : headB; b = b ? b.next : headA; they meet at intersection (or both at null). Elegant alignment trick.

dummy-head-merge.21: Merge 2 Sorted Lists. Dummy head; tail=dummy; pick smaller head and append; advance.
dummy-head-merge.23: Merge K Sorted Lists. Same idea + min-heap of stream heads (O(N log K)). OR divide-and-conquer pairwise merge.
dummy-head-merge.203: Remove LL Elements. Dummy head simplifies the case where head itself needs removal; walk, skip on match.
dummy-head-merge.708: Insert into Sorted Cyclic List. Walk one loop finding the right slot (handles min-max wrap and uniform-value cases).

list-digit-arithmetic.2: Add Two Numbers (LSB-first lists). Walk both with carry; create new node per digit; dummy-head merge style.
list-digit-arithmetic.445: Add Two Numbers II (MSB-first). Reverse both (or use 2 stacks) then same carry-walk.
list-digit-arithmetic.369: Plus One Linked List. Reverse, add 1 with carry, reverse back. Or recurse returning carry.

dll-cache-design.146: LRU Cache. HashMap key→DLL-node; on get/put move node to head (most recent); evict from tail on overflow.
dll-cache-design.460: LFU Cache. HashMap key→node; HashMap freq→DLL-of-nodes; minFreq tracker; on access bump node's freq + move to new freq-list.
dll-cache-design.432: All O`one Data Structure. Doubly-linked list of count-buckets; HashMap key→bucket; getMin/Max in O(1) via head/tail.
dll-cache-design.1756: Design Most Recently Used Queue. Linked list of buckets (sqrt decomposition) or order-statistic tree for O(sqrt n) or O(log n) fetch.

min-stack-design.155: Min Stack. Pair every push with running min; pop returns and discards both.
min-stack-design.716: Max Stack. Pair with running max; popMax requires O(n) re-stack-up of larger items.
min-stack-design.232: Queue via 2 Stacks. push→in-stack; pop→out-stack (refill from in when empty). Amortised O(1).
min-stack-design.225: Stack via 2 Queues. Either O(n) push (rotate after) or O(n) pop (move all but last).
min-stack-design.895: Max Freq Stack. Map<val, count> + Map<freq, stack>; push bumps; pop takes from top of maxFreq stack.
min-stack-design.1381: Stack With Increment Op. Lazy increment array; flush to popped element.

validate-stack-seq.946: Validate Stack Sequences. Simulate with aux stack: push pushed[i]; while top==popped[j] pop and ++j; at end stack empty ⇒ valid.
validate-stack-seq.735: Asteroid Collision. Stack of survivors; on negative, pop while top > 0 && top < |cur| (smaller positives destroyed); annihilate on equal.
validate-stack-seq.901: Online Stock Span. Monotonic-decreasing stack of (price, span); on cur, pop+sum spans of all ≤ cur; push (cur, accSpan+1).
validate-stack-seq.1441: Build Array With Stack Ops. Walk 1..n; push 'Push'; if target absent also push 'Pop'.

queue-from-stacks.232: Implement Queue via Stacks. in-stack for push; out-stack for pop; refill out from in when empty. Amortised O(1).
queue-from-stacks.225: Implement Stack via Queues. Push-O(n): enqueue then rotate (n-1) times so new is at front.
queue-from-stacks.622: Design Circular Queue. Fixed-size array + head + count.
queue-from-stacks.641: Design Circular Deque. Array + head + tail (or count) with modular indexing.

moving-average-stream.346: Moving Average from Stream. Bounded queue + running sum; on overflow evict front and adjust sum.
moving-average-stream.933: Number of Recent Calls. Queue of timestamps; evict t < cur-3000; return queue size.
moving-average-stream.1352: Product of Last K Numbers. Prefix-product array; on 0 reset; query uses ratio.

path-sum-dfs.112: Path Sum exists. DFS subtract; at leaf check remaining==0.
path-sum-dfs.113: Path Sum II — collect all. Backtracking on the path list.
path-sum-dfs.437: Path Sum III (any-to-any descendant). Prefix-sum hashmap on DFS path: map[curPrefix-target] gives count.
path-sum-dfs.129: Sum Root to Leaf Numbers. DFS carrying accumulated number 10*acc+val; at leaf add to total.
path-sum-dfs.257: All Root-to-Leaf Paths. DFS with path-string accumulator; collect on leaf.

construct-from-traversals.105: From Preorder+Inorder. Pre[0]=root; find in inorder → left/right subtree spans; recurse with index map.
construct-from-traversals.106: From Postorder+Inorder. Post[-1]=root; same split via inorder.
construct-from-traversals.889: From Preorder+Postorder. Pre[1]=left-root → find in post to size left subtree; not unique in general but works for full BTs.

serialize-tree.297: Serialize/Deserialize BT. Pre-order with 'null' markers so structure round-trips.
serialize-tree.449: Serialize/Deserialize BST. BST property lets you skip null markers (use bounds on deserialize).
serialize-tree.572: Subtree of Another Tree. Serialize both with unique delimiters; substring check (KMP-able).
serialize-tree.652: Find Duplicate Subtrees. Post-order serialize each subtree; HashMap<serialization, count>.

inorder-bst.98: Validate BST. Inorder walk; check prev < cur. (Or bounds-DFS.)
inorder-bst.230: Kth Smallest BST. Inorder iterative; pop K-1 nodes; K-th is answer.
inorder-bst.173: BST Iterator. Stack of left-spine; next pops + advances to right subtree's left-spine.
inorder-bst.285: Inorder Successor BST. Walk: if val > p.val candidate=val, go left; else go right.
inorder-bst.270: Closest Value BST. Walk root→leaf, track closest seen; choose direction by value comparison.
inorder-bst.783: Min Diff in BST. Inorder + track prev value; update min |cur-prev|.
inorder-bst.99: Recover BST. Inorder traversal finds two swapped nodes; swap their values.

bst-bounds-validate.98: Validate BST. def f(n, lo, hi): if !n: ok; if !(lo<n.val<hi): fail; recurse left (lo,val), right (val,hi).
bst-bounds-validate.333: Largest BST Subtree. Post-order returning (isBST, size, min, max); combine at each node.

bst-lca.235: LCA of BST. Walk: both < node go left; both > go right; else node IS LCA. O(h) iterative.

bst-insert-delete.701: Insert BST. Recurse on comparator branch; place at null leaf.
bst-insert-delete.450: Delete Node BST. Recurse to find; on hit with 2 children swap with inorder successor then delete; ≤1 child splice.
bst-insert-delete.700: Search BST. Trivial recurse on comparator branch.
bst-insert-delete.938: Range Sum BST. Recurse but PRUNE: skip left if node.val < low; skip right if > high.

trie-basic.208: Implement Trie. Each node = Map<char, TrieNode> + isWord. insert/search/startsWith all walk the chain.
trie-basic.211: Word Dictionary (with '.'). On '.' branch into ALL children; else descend matching child.
trie-basic.1166: Design File System. Trie keyed on path segments; value at terminal.
trie-basic.588: Design In-Memory FS. Trie of path segments + per-node files (string → content).

trie-wildcard.211: Word Dictionary. DFS the trie; on '.' try all children; else single descend.
trie-wildcard.676: Magic Dictionary. Pre-build trie of words; on search try changing exactly one char at each position.
trie-wildcard.745: Prefix and Suffix Search. Insert (suffix + '#' + word) for each suffix; query (suffix + '#' + prefix).

cc-dfs-uf.200: Number of Islands. For each '1' DFS-mark then ++count. (Also dfs-grid-flood.)
cc-dfs-uf.547: Number of Provinces. DFS adjacency matrix.
cc-dfs-uf.323: Number of CC Undirected. UF on each edge; final root count.
cc-dfs-uf.695: Max Area Island. DFS returning subtree area; track max.
cc-dfs-uf.130: Surrounded Regions. DFS from boundary 'O' marking 'safe'; flip remaining 'O' to 'X'.
cc-dfs-uf.1971: Find if Path Exists. UF union each edge; check source/target same root.

cycle-3color.207: Course Schedule cycle detect. WHITE→GRAY (in-stack)→BLACK (done); back-edge to GRAY = cycle.
cycle-3color.802: Find Eventual Safe States. Reverse 3-color: nodes whose DFS doesn't hit GRAY are safe.

bipartite.785: Bipartite Check. BFS/DFS coloring alternating; conflict ⇒ not bipartite. Handle disconnected.
bipartite.886: Possible Bipartition. Build graph from dislike pairs; same coloring check.

dag-longest-path.329: Longest Increasing Path Matrix. Memoized DFS (= DP on implicit DAG of '<' edges).
dag-longest-path.1857: Largest Color Value DAG. Topo + DP over count[v][color].
dag-longest-path.2050: Parallel Courses III. Topo + DP — finish[v] = max(prereqFinish) + duration[v].
dag-longest-path.2127: Max Employees Invited. Each node's outdegree 1 (functional graph); decompose into cycles + chains feeding them.

mst.1135: Min Cost Connect Cities. Kruskal: sort edges, union if disjoint. Or Prim with min-heap from any start.
mst.1584: Min Cost Connect Points. Same — Kruskal on n² edges or Prim avoiding edge enumeration.
mst.1489: Critical & Pseudo-Critical Edges in MST. Baseline MST weight; for each edge, retest including/excluding to classify.

ancestor-reachability.1462: Course Schedule IV. Build closure: ancestors[v] = ∪ ancestors of preds + preds themselves. Query in O(1).
ancestor-reachability.2192: All Ancestors of Each Node in DAG. Topo order; carry ancestor-set forward (union as you process).
ancestor-reachability.851: Loud and Rich. DFS/DP — answer[v] = quietest among {v} ∪ {answer of each richer-than-v predecessor}.
ancestor-reachability.802: Eventual Safe States. Topo from sinks (out-deg-0 in reverse).

euler-tour.332: Reconstruct Itinerary. Hierholzer with sorted PQ of neighbours per node (lex-smallest); post-order append; reverse.
euler-tour.753: Cracking the Safe. De Bruijn sequence via Eulerian on (n-1)-tuple → digit graph.
euler-tour.2097: Valid Arrangement of Pairs. Eulerian path on directed multigraph of (a→b) edges.

tarjan-bridges.1192: Critical Connections. Tarjan: disc[]/low[]; edge (u,v) is bridge iff low[v] > disc[u].
tarjan-bridges.1568: Min Days Disconnect Island. Either 0/1/2 — check connected, then check articulation, then it's 2.

mat-rotate.48: Rotate Image 90° CW. Transpose (swap a[i][j]↔a[j][i]) then reverse each row. O(n²) time, O(1) space.
mat-rotate.189: Rotate Array (1D variant) — triple reverse. Listed here for cross-link.

mat-spiral.54: Spiral Matrix. Maintain (top, bottom, left, right); walk row/col and shrink bounds.
mat-spiral.59: Spiral Matrix II — generate. Same loop but write 1..n² instead of read.
mat-spiral.885: Spiral Matrix III. Walk in spiral covering even out-of-bound cells; collect cells in bounds.

mat-set-zeros.73: Set Matrix Zeroes. Use first row + col as flags; handle them last. O(1) extra space.

mat-grid-dfs-bfs.695: Max Area Island. DFS returning subtree area.
mat-grid-dfs-bfs.130: Surrounded Regions. Flood from boundary 'O' marking safe.
mat-grid-dfs-bfs.463: Island Perimeter. Count cell-edges adjacent to water or grid boundary. (No DFS needed; one pass.)
mat-grid-dfs-bfs.733: Flood Fill. Plain BFS/DFS replacing color.
mat-grid-dfs-bfs.1254: Closed Islands. Like 130 but count; flood from boundary, count remaining components.

two-heap-median.480: Sliding Window Median. Two heaps + lazy deletion map for out-of-window evictions.

decode-string.736: Lisp Expression Eval. Parser with environment stack for let-bindings.
